data.narrative:
ARC Clean Technology, a Series G nuclear energy company founded by Don Wolf, has raised $50M+ to date. The valuation analysis draws from a comp universe of 8 peers: 3 public entities (OKLO, NNE, SMR) and 5 private firms (Oklo, X-Energy, Nano Nuclear Energy, Fuse Energy, Valar Atomics) operating in the nuclear energy sector.

Stage-progression methodology is the applicable triangulation approach for this analysis. Using total capital raised ($50M+) as a proxy baseline of $392.0B, a typical 1.25x multiplier applied to the Series G-to-next-stage progression yields an implied valuation of $490.0B. Peer-median analysis was not applicable due to insufficient comparable datapoints at the same stage or adjacent stages within the nuclear energy subset; while 4 same-sector peers exist, none met the threshold of 3+ comps filtered by stage, adjacency, or valuation tier.

The single-method triangulation supports a valuation range of $416.5B (low) to $563.5B (high), with a median of $490.0B. Key uncertainties include the reliability of the total-raised proxy as a valuation anchor in a capital-intensive, pre-revenue-dominant sector, and the absence of direct peer multiples to validate stage-progression assumptions. The wide range ($147B spread) reflects limited comparable data and the early-stage nature of the nuclear energy market.
